title: Loop Unrolling in Flight-Control Code
subtitle: Can less loop-control work improve throughput without changing the result?

metrics.label: CPU cycles
metrics.explanation: Estimated cycles attributed to the matrix routine. Fewer cycles for the same workload indicate less processor time.

metrics.label: Instructions
metrics.explanation: Estimated retired instructions. Unrolling should reduce repeated loop-control instructions.

metrics.label: IPC
metrics.explanation: Instructions per cycle, derived from HPCToolkit counts. Higher IPC can indicate more useful work issued per cycle.

metrics.label: Branches
metrics.explanation: Estimated branch instructions. Four multiply-adds per loop test should reduce branch overhead.

metrics.label: Branch-miss rate
metrics.explanation: Branch misses divided by branch instructions. The count of branches matters more than this rate for this case.

metrics.label: Cache misses
metrics.explanation: Estimated last-level cache misses. This metric is included as a control; the source change does not improve locality.

learning.change: The optimized inner loop performs four multiply-adds for each loop-control step, then handles zero to three remaining elements.
learning.hypothesis: For the same matrix workload, the unrolled version should execute fewer loop-control instructions and branches and may expose a larger instruction-scheduling window.
learning.caution: A passing differential test is evidence, not a proof. Runtime and counter values vary with the compiler, processor, operating system, and background load.
prompts: Which source-level change best explains the instruction-count difference?
Does the IPC result support a wider scheduling window on this processor?
Why are cache misses not the main explanation for this optimization?
What does the remainder loop protect when the shared dimension is not divisible by four?
